packages.name: @kiln/kiln
packages.purpose: The Kiln compiler: a generic IR/rewrite/fork-decision core (src/core) and a GPU compiler stack on it (src/std): nn/tensor dialects, loop fusion, tile scheduling with a cost model, kernel materialisation, CUDA/WGSL/simulator emitters, devices, measurement records, evidence store, tuner and kiln-program/1 export.
packages.notes: Plain ES modules, no build, no types. Deps: acorn 8.19.0, @kiln/evidence (TS source). Tests: 13 node scripts run by scripts/run-node-tests.mjs.

packages.name: runtime/webgpu
packages.purpose: Browser launcher for kiln-program/1: KilnWebGpuProgram.create(device, program), write, encode, run, destroy.
packages.notes: Imports nothing from the repo. Only consumer: runtime/test/webgpu-roundtrip.mjs (headless Chrome).

packages.name: runtime/python
packages.purpose: Python launcher for kiln-program/1 with two backends: wgpu-py (WgpuProgram) and CUDA via ctypes driver API + NVRTC (CudaProgram, allocate=False for caller-owned memory). CLI: kiln_launch.py check <fixtures> --backend.
packages.notes: numpy required; wgpu or libcuda/libnvrtc (system or torch wheel). runtime/test/fixtures.mjs is counted here: it builds the fixture programs both launchers and the kiln-perf image check.

packages.name: runner
packages.purpose: CUDA execution on a GPU host: kiln_runner.py (nvcc harness, kiln-bundle/1 -> kiln-results/1, runs inside the kiln-perf image) and kiln_driver.py (kiln-driver/1 HTTP executor: blobs, jobs as Docker containers, per-GPU flock, events, archives, self-replace).
packages.notes: Standard library only (+ nvcc, docker, nvidia-smi on the host). No test file in the repo is named for either.

packages.name: runner/docker
packages.purpose: The kiln-perf image (Ubuntu 24.04, CUDA 13.0 nvcc + NVRTC, numpy, optional Nsight Compute) with the runner, the Python launcher, prebuilt fixtures, kiln-probe and kiln-selftest; plus the perf-lab-cpu image.
packages.notes: build.sh refuses a dirty tree over runner, runtime/python, runtime/test, packages/kiln/src, apps/workbench/src and apps/workbench/presets, because fixtures are compiled from the workbench.

packages.name: imports/kiln-workbench-src
packages.purpose: The original Kiln Workbench as received: one app/ (core, std, ui, agent, tests), presets, runner, docs, built HTML and the zip it came in. Frozen; not imported by live code.
packages.notes: 116 tracked files under imports/ including kiln-workbench-src.zip (1.09 MB). 11948 lines excluding dist, built HTML and package-lock; app/src alone 8187 lines.

duplications.title: kernel identity hash: loop, tile, kernel and gpu dialects plus programOf
duplications.description: Five hand-written copies of the kernel identity formula hash(`loop|expr|shape|inputs`). The loop.kernel copy keys inputs by shape only; the other four use inKey(shape, dtype). The schedule fork is keyed while the node is a loop.kernel, so a u8 kernel's fork key equals the f32 kernel's identity while programOf reports a different, dtype-aware identity (probe: fork key 302w2uv760, kernel identity 2dbf6f6auuk; activationOf says 'no schedule fork decided this kernel').
duplications.suggested_consolidation: One exported kernelIdentity({expr, shape, inShapes, inDtypes}) in std (or on the loop dialect) used by all five sites; a test that traces the same kernel with f32 and u8 inputs and asserts fork key == program identity.

duplications.title: CUDA entry symbol and C name derivation
duplications.description: The rule 'kernel name -> C identifier' and 'find the __global__ function in a source' is written six times in three languages; export renames the entry with a regex after emission.

locations.note: cname used in the emitted signature
symbolOf, comment says 'as the emitters print it'
compiles with entry = kernel name (relies on renameCuda)

duplications.suggested_consolidation: Export cname/symbolOf once from emit.js and import it in export.js/records.js; carry the entry symbol as data (bundle and program kernels already have a name field) instead of re-parsing sources in the runner and exec.

duplications.title: seeded kernel input generator (mulberry32) in JS and in the CUDA harness
duplications.description: Kernel inputs are generated by mulberry32 in the workbench and re-implemented in C++ inside the runner's harness so CUDA results can be checked against the page's reference at sampled indices.

locations.note: HARNESS C++ mulberry32, 'exactly as the workbench (kernelInputs)'

duplications.suggested_consolidation: Keep both (two languages are inherent) but pin them with a shared golden vector test: N draws for seed S, f32 and u8 mappings, checked by packages/kiln/test and by kiln-selftest.

duplications.title: launcher fixture input formula in JS and Python
duplications.description: Fixture inputs h = (i*2654435761 + s*40503) mod 2^32 are generated by the fixture builder and again by the Python launcher's checker.
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Store the inputs in the fixture files (they are small) or keep the formula with a golden-vector check.

duplications.title: WebGPU program execution: workbench device vs runtime launcher
duplications.description: Two implementations of 'upload inputs, bind, dispatch, read back' for compiled kernels: the workbench's measurement device and the standalone kiln-program/1 launcher. Both pack u8 one byte per element padded to words; the 65535 grid fold is computed in three places.
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Let WebGpuDevice run kernels through KilnWebGpuProgram (or a shared lower-level helper) and compute the fold once (export's dispatch), so the measured path and the shipped launcher are the same code.

duplications.title: kiln-program/1 launch limits check: TypeScript and Python
duplications.description: unsupportedReason/unsupported_reason check the same device limits (workgroups per dimension, invocations, storage buffer size, workgroup storage) in each launcher.
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Acceptable per-language duplication; document the limit list in the kiln-program/1 schema.

duplications.title: CUDA compilation wrappers (NVRTC via ctypes, nvcc subprocess)
duplications.description: Two ctypes NVRTC wrappers and two nvcc invocations.

locations.note: _Cuda: driver API + NVRTC, cubin else PTX

duplications.suggested_consolidation: Retire apps/workbench/test/cuda_check.py in favour of kiln_launch.py (its _Cuda already compiles and launches).

duplications.title: nvidia-smi querying in runner, driver and probe
duplications.description: Three Python programs build their own nvidia-smi --query-gpu argument lists and parse CSV; the compute-apps query is the same string in two of them; the driver itself has two field lists.

locations.note: GPU_SAMPLER_FIELDS, gpus, gpu_counters, compute_apps, gpu_now, sampler

duplications.suggested_consolidation: A small shared smi.py (fields, CSV parsing, [N/A] handling) vendored into the kiln-perf image and the driver.

duplications.title: measurement protocol defaults {reps 7, warmup 3, launches 20, seed 1}
duplications.description: The default WebGPU measurement protocol is a literal in three places; the CUDA runner has different defaults (reps 50, warmup 5) that the bundle normally overrides.
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Export DEFAULT_PROTOCOL from std/devices.js and import it in the workbench.

duplications.title: flatKnobs helper in records.js and the workbench server client
duplications.description: Byte-identical one-line function (verified by string comparison).

duplications.title: GPU target specs and hand-written target lists
duplications.description: SPECS in std/targets.js is the compiler's source of truth; the probe prints specs in its shape (copied in by hand), the CUDA mapping and host device default to rtx5090, and three literal lists repeat the target names.
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Generate help text and agent/reference lists from SPECS; store measured specs as data next to SPECS.

duplications.title: imported original Kiln Workbench snapshot vs its split homes
duplications.description: imports/kiln-workbench-src/kiln-workbench is a full frozen copy of the compiler, UI, presets, tests and runner that now live in packages/kiln, apps/workbench and runner. ix.js, script.js, emmy.js, loop.js and six tests are byte-identical; kiln.js differs by 52 diff lines, devices.js by 383, store.js by 188, tune.js by 91.
duplications.suggested_consolidation: Keep only the zip (or a git tag) as provenance and delete the expanded tree.

complexity_hotspots.reason: One file holds the IR, dialect registry, patterns, forks, decision policies, pipelines and the Run engine (761-1094) that schedules passes, matches rules, expands forks, records decisions, journals steps with periodic snapshots and emits UI events. Five pieces of module-level state (SCOPES, METHODS, DIALECTS, GID, RID).
complexity_hotspots.metric: LOC; god object (Run ~330 lines, 20 methods); module globals
complexity_hotspots.suggestion: Split Run into pass scheduler, fork decider and journal; move registries into a context object.

complexity_hotspots.reason: HTTP handler, job queue and recovery, plan validation, content-addressed blobs, Docker orchestration, per-GPU flock with idle-window conditions, nvidia-smi sampler sidecar, archiving and self-replacement in one process and file.
complexity_hotspots.suggestion: Separate the HTTP surface from the job engine and the GPU lock; keep it standard-library only.

complexity_hotspots.reason: The analytic cost model (timeModel 152-194, estimate) is the only scheduling prior; decisions are explained only as 'model' plus the knob map. Knob legality, launch geometry and register estimates live in the same file.
complexity_hotspots.suggestion: Isolate the cost model behind an interface with its own tests.

complexity_hotspots.reason: Three emitters in one file; toSim generates a lockstep SIMT simulator as JS source (one small function per statement, masks per depth, instrumented counters) and compiles it with new Function.
complexity_hotspots.suggestion: Keep, but give the simulator its own module and tests.

complexity_hotspots.reason: Hash-consed expressions in a module-level INTERN table capped at 400000 entries plus a FREE WeakMap and a global RV counter; fusion with a blow-up guard; LICM scheduling.
complexity_hotspots.suggestion: Scope the intern table to a compilation.

complexity_hotspots.reason: Measurement protocol, timer quantum, deadlines and a second WebGPU execution path (runOnce) next to the standalone launcher.
Hand-written ctypes bindings of the CUDA driver API and NVRTC with library discovery (env, system, torch wheel) and caller-owned memory mode.
complexity_hotspots.suggestion: Keep standalone; add a schema file for kiln-program/1.

facts.subject: @kiln/kiln
facts.fact: @kiln/kiln has no index or root export: package.json exports only ./core/* and ./std/*, so every consumer deep-imports individual files.

facts.subject: @kiln/kiln
facts.fact: @kiln/kiln depends on acorn 8.19.0 and on @kiln/evidence, whose exports point at TypeScript source, so std modules that touch evidence need a TS-stripping runtime (Node 26 native type stripping).

facts.subject: @kiln/kiln
facts.fact: @kiln/kiln is plain JavaScript ES modules with no build step and no type declarations; apps/server declares '@kiln/kiln/*' as an untyped ambient module.

facts.subject: @kiln/kiln
facts.fact: The only core -> std import is core/script.js importing ../std/index.js; the rest of core/ depends on nothing in the repo.

facts.subject: @kiln/kiln
facts.fact: @kiln/kiln tests are 13 standalone node scripts run one process each by scripts/run-node-tests.mjs; std modules are covered end to end, not per module.

facts.subject: @kiln/kiln
facts.fact: Size: core 1508 lines (kiln.js 1152, ix.js 241, util.js 76, script.js 39), std 3028 lines over 16 files, tests 855 lines.

facts.subject: @kiln/kiln
facts.fact: apps/server uses @kiln/kiln only in a test (decide.test.ts imports k, N, pipeline, SPECS, EvidenceStore, activationOf, programOf); apps/workbench imports it from 23 files.

facts.subject: @kiln/kiln
facts.fact: scripts/kiln-export.mjs and runtime/test/fixtures.mjs import the compiler by relative path ../packages/kiln/src/... and import compileScript/endToEnd from apps/workbench/src/compile.js, so tooling depends on the app.

facts.subject: packages/kiln/src/core/kiln.js
facts.fact: Dialects register into a module-level DIALECTS map and dialect methods into a module-level METHODS map (name -> list of {dialect, fn}); a Proxy HANDLER resolves x.method() on Values through it.

facts.subject: packages/kiln/src/core/kiln.js
facts.fact: Graph building uses a module-level SCOPES stack; node ids come from a global GID counter and rule ids from a global RID counter.

facts.subject: packages/kiln/src/core/kiln.js
facts.fact: Node objects are frozen; Graph provides clone, addNode, replaceUses, users, topo, dce, find/findAll, key, print and eval.

facts.subject: packages/kiln/src/core/kiln.js
facts.fact: Rule.from()/to() recover pattern variable names by parsing the lambda's source text with a regex (paramNames); minified or transpiled rules would break binding.

facts.subject: packages/kiln/src/core/kiln.js
facts.fact: Pass modes are fixpoint, once and ordered-once, with a cap of 4000 rewrite steps per pass.

facts.subject: packages/kiln/src/core/kiln.js
facts.fact: expandFork refuses fork trees with more than 20000 options.

facts.subject: packages/kiln/src/core/kiln.js
facts.fact: Decision policies: decide.first, pinned (partial pins allowed), random, cost, chain, exactly, evidence (optionStats with minReps and separated intervals), strict.

facts.subject: packages/kiln/src/core/kiln.js
facts.fact: Run.recordStep stores a delta per rewrite and a full graph snapshot every 48 rewrites; stepGraph(i) and diff(i) rebuild any step from them.

facts.subject: packages/kiln/src/core/kiln.js
facts.fact: Run.checkIr enforces that only the dialects an IR declares remain at its checkpoint when the IR is strict.

facts.subject: packages/kiln/src/core/kiln.js
facts.fact: runPass resumes a fixpoint pass incrementally from the last rewritten node rather than rescanning the graph.

facts.subject: packages/kiln/src/core/kiln.js
facts.fact: unifiedDiff is an O(n*m) LCS over printed graph lines.

facts.subject: packages/kiln/src/core/kiln.js
